de4_land_text.topic: Nick Land, The Dark Enlightenment (2012 serial; 2014 e-book compilation): structure, credits to Moldbug, Thiel citation, key passages

claims.text: The serial ran in ten instalments, Part 1 (2 March 2012) to Part 4f (20 July 2012); the 2014 e-book is a verbatim compilation
Part 1 opens with the April 2009 Cato Unbound discussion and quotes Thiel: 'I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible' (e-book p. 2)

Part 1 names the current 'recognizably Hobbesian, a coherent dark enlightenment' and asks, 'From Thomas Hobbes to Hans-Hermann Hoppe and beyond', how sovereign power can be prevented from devouring society (p. 3); quotes Hoppe's king-as-owner vs democratic caretaker with usufruct (p. 4)

Land calls Moldbug 'supreme Sith Lord of the neoreactionaries'; says Moldbug's 'formative influences are Austro-libertarian, but that's all over'; quotes his neocameralism definition ('a state is a business which owns a country'); 'Moldbug calls it the Cathedral'; 'No voice, free exit' (pp. 5–6)
Land quotes Moldbug: neocameralism 'has never been tried'; closest equivalents Frederick the Great and Hong Kong, Singapore and Dubai, 'weak only in political freedom' (p. 6)

Part 2: democracy 'consumes progress'; study it as 'general parasitology' (p. 11); Part 3: 'Whatever is subsidized is promoted' (p. 18); 'No democracy could accept this, which means that every democracy will fail' (p. 18); regime table (p. 20)

Part 4 (pp. 23–28): white nationalism as a 'decaying orbit' into a 'black hole'; the antisemitic turn called 'the labyrinth, the trap'; Hitler as 'mirror Messiah'; Part 4a white flight 'all exit and no voice' (p. 31); Part 4b 'sheer Gnostic delirium' and 'Violence on a genocidal scale is required to even approximate to a practical egalitarian program' (p. 40); Saletan and Millman quoted (pp. 43–44)

Part 4c: 'progressivism has no enemies to the left' credited to Moldbug (p. 47); 'Escape is racist' (p. 51); Part 4d: Mises Institute, Ron Paul newsletters, Rothbard on HBD, Palmer vs Rockwell/Hoppe; 'liberty has no future in the Anglophone world outside the prospect of secession' (pp. 54–55)

Part 4e: three futures, Modernity 2.0 from a Chinese core 'by far the most encouraging'; wish-list: replace representative democracy, downsize government, hard money and abolition of central banking, end of macroeconomic discretion (pp. 57–58); Part 4f: Cathedral as 'Media-Academic complex' named by Moldbug; bionic horizon; Campbell's elite genetic self-engineering and speciation (pp. 61–64)
MacDougald: the c.27,000-word essay published on thedarkenlightenment.com; Land's corporate-dictatorship prescriptions adopted from Moldbug

de4_land_life.topic: Nick Land: Warwick, CCRU, accelerationism and its split, Shanghai

claims.text: Land, born 1962, lectured in philosophy at Warwick 1987–1998 and resigned in 1998

Sadie Plant founded the CCRU at Warwick in 1995; after she resigned in 1997 Land took over; his student Robin Mackay recalled him living in his office and rarely sleeping; Land later said of that writing, 'I don't even remember writing half of those things'
Benjamin Noys named the trajectory 'accelerationism' in The Persistence of the Negative (2010); Deleuze and Guattari's 'accelerate the process' is the cited inspiration

Srnicek and Williams' 2013 manifesto: Land had 'a myopic yet hypnotising belief' that 'capitalist speed alone could generate a global transition towards unparalleled technological singularity'; the platform of neoliberalism 'does not need to be destroyed. It needs to be repurposed towards common ends'
Land disavowed left accelerationism; wrote 'Neoreaction is Accelerationism with a flat tire'; resurfaced in the new millennium as a journalist in Shanghai
Neo-fascist and white-supremacist networks use 'accelerationism' for accelerating racial conflict through violence; Beauchamp: Land's technocapitalist ideas otherwise unrelated
Brassier (Guardian 2017): Land has gone from 'Politics is dead' to 'completely old-fashioned, standard reactionary stuff'; Fisher: 'Land was our Nietzsche'

Spectator, 21 Oct 2025: Land in Shanghai, in his sixties; Xenosystems (2013–2017 writings) published by Passage Press; Andreessen lists him as a 'patron saint'; Land calls China's mix 'the greatest political engine of social and economic development the world has ever known'
#Accelerate reader (Mackay and Avanessian, Urbanomic 2014) placed Land in its 'Cyberculture' section with Iain Hamilton Grant and Sadie Plant

de4_hard.topic: Land's hard passages and critics: hyper-racism (2014), HBD, critics

claims.text: Land's post 'Hyper-Racism' appeared on the Alternative Right blog on 4 October 2014; the term does not appear in the 2012 serial

Haider: in that editorial Land named his theory 'hyperracism'; treated socioeconomic status as 'a strong proxy for IQ'; wrote of a 'genetically self-filtering elite' and that 'space colonization will inevitably function as a highly-selective genetic filter'; Haider: Land 'simply carried the mainstream ideology to its inexorable result'
Haider: 'human biodiversity' used as a euphemism for scientific racism; Jonathan Marks: 'the heredity of race is not genetic, but social'

Sandifer (Neoreaction a Basilisk, 2017): gave the work 'as much intellectual respect as I could before I took it out back and shot it'; 'Their ideas make no sense if you look at them under any scrutiny whatsoever'
